To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
ZP3- and ZP2-binding sites on mouse sperm are distinct in their distribution, numbers, and affinities, are specific for ZP3 or ZP2, respectively, and are regulated by capacitation and maturing sperm.
ZP3 binding to sperm is restricted to the acrosomal and postacrosomal regions of the head, whereas ZP2 binding to sperm is limited to the postacrosome.
mouse sperm express saturable, specific, and calcium-dependent binding sites for Zp3 and ZP3.

the identification and characterization of ZP3- and ZP2-binding sites on mouse sperm.
the identification of ZP3- and ZP2-specific sites on sperm.
identifying and characterizing the binding sites on sperm that interact with the ZP.

the binding of ZP2 and ZP3 to sperm requires capacitation and maturing of the sperm.
mouse sperm express saturable binding sites for Zp3 and Zp2.
mouse sperm express distinct, saturable, specific, calcium-dependent, and regulated binding sites for the glycoproteins ZP3 and the glycoprotein ZP2.

mouse sperm possess distinct, saturable, specific, and calcium-regulated binding sites for ZPs.
